name: Queen's Gambit Declined
summary: The classical answer to 1.d4: hold the centre with ...e6 and ...d5, develop, then free the game with ...c5 or ...e5.

notes.8: ...Be7 breaks the pin before it hurts; ...Nbd7 and ...c6 come next.
notes.14: ...c6 supports d5 and prepares the freeing plan: ...dxc4, ...Nd5 and ...e5 (Capablanca's manoeuvre).
notes.16: ...dxc4 only after Bd3: the bishop loses a tempo coming to c4.
notes.18: ...Nd5 offers trades; with fewer pieces the cramped position breathes.
notes.24: ...e5: the freeing break. Black has equalised; play ...exd4, ...Nf6 or ...Nb6 and activity on the e-file.

notes.8: ...exd5 keeps the structure: Black gets the half-open e-file, White will try the minority attack with b4-b5.
notes.10: ...c6 solidifies d5 and meets Qc2 ideas against h7 with ...Be7 and ...Nbd7.
notes.18: ...Re8 and ...Nf8 is the standard regrouping: the knight guards h7 and can go to g6 or e6.
notes.22: ...Be6 completes development. Plans: ...Rc8 and ...c5, or ...Ne4 to trade pieces; against b4-b5 answer with ...a6 and ...b5 in time.

notes.12: ...dxc4 takes the pawn now that the bishop is on g2 and can't recapture quickly.
notes.16: ...b5 keeps the extra pawn for a while and gains space; the bishop goes to b7 to challenge g2.
notes.20: ...Be4 hits the queen and blocks the long diagonal for a moment.
notes.22: ...Nbd7, then ...c5 or ...Rc8 and ...c5: Black returns the pawn for full development and easy play.
